title: Use the Continuity Equation
text: The continuity equation states $$Q=A_{1}v_{1}=A_{2}v_{2},$$ where $$A_{1}$$ and $$v_{1}$$ are the cross-sectional area and speed of the water in the hose and $$A_{2}$$ and $$v_{2}$$ are the cross-sectional area and speed of the water in the nozzle.

title: Calculate the Cross-Sectional Area $$A_{1}$$
text: The area of a circle is $$A=\pi{}r**2.$$ For the fire hose with a diameter of $$9.00\, \text{cm}, $$ what is $$A_{1}$$ (in $$\text{m}**2)$$?

title: Calculate the Cross-Sectional Area $$A_{2}$$
text: The area of a circle is $$A=\pi{}r**2.$$ For the nozzle with a diameter of $$3.00\, \text{cm}, $$ what is $$A_{2}$$ (in $$\text{m}**2)$$?

title: Use Bernoulli’s Equation
text: Bernoulli’s equation is $$P_{1}+\tfrac12\rho{}v_{1}**2=P_{2}+\tfrac12\rho{}v_{2}**2.$$ Find the speeds with $$v=\frac{Q}{A}, $$ then rearrange for the pressure drop $$\Delta{}P=P_{1}-P_{2},$$ using $$\rho=1000\,\text{kg/m}**3$$ for water.
